Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Rajeev Misra,J.
1. Heard Mr. A.C. Srivastava, the learned counsel for applicant and the learned A.G.A. for State.
2. Perused the record.

3. This repeat application for bail has been filed by applicant-Ikrar, seeking his enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 144 of 2021, under Sections 498A, 323, 304-B IPC and Sections 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station- Kithore, District- Meerut during the pendency of trial i.e. Session Trial No. 1138 of 2021 (State Vs. Ikrar) now pending in the Court of Additional District Judge, Court No.2, Meerut.

sentences.text: 1 4. The first bail application of applicant was rejected by this Court for default vide order dated 14.03.2022 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 3535 of 2022 (Ikrar Vs. State of U.P. and another).

sentences.text:
For ready reference, the same is reproduced hereinunder:-
"Case called out in revised list.
No one appears on behalf of applicant to press this application for bail.
Learned A.G.A. and Mr. Rajiv Kumar Mishra, learned counsel for first informant are present.

In view of above, present application for bail is dismissed for want of prosecution."
5.

Record shows that in respect of an incidents, which are alleged to have occurred from 20.02.2019 to 01.05.2021, a prompt FIR dated 01.05.2021 was lodged by first informant-Jameel (father of the deceased) and was registered as Case Crime No. 144 of 2021, under Sections 498A, 323, 304-B IPC and Sections 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station- Kithore, District- Meerut.
In the aforesaid FIR, two persons namely Ikrar husband of the deceased (applicant herein) and Ruksana (mother-in-law of the deceased) have been nominated as named accused.
6. The gravamen of the allegations made in the FIR to the effect that marriage of Rizwana (daughter of the first informant) was solemnized with Ikrar (applicant herein) on 20.02.2019.
The FIR further records that named accused continuously assaulted the daughter of the first informant.
Ultiamtely the daughter of the first informant was put to death on 01.05.2021.
7. After above-mentioned FIR was lodged, Investigating Officer proceeded with statutory investigation of concerned case crime number in terms of Chapter-XII Cr.P.C.
The inquest (Panchayatnama) of the body of deceased was conducted on 01.05.2021.
In the opinion of the witnesses of inquest (Panch witnesses), the nature of death of deceased was categorized as suicidal.
Subsequent to above, the post mortem of the body of deceased was conducted.
In the opinion of autopsy surgeon who conducted autopsy of the body of deceased, the cause of death of the deceased was opined as Asphyxia due to ante-mortem hanging.

The autopsy surgeon found following ante-mortem injuries on the body of deceased:-
1. Ligature mark is in the form of presure abrasion, oblique and incomplete measure 32cm x 2cm present on neck, 2cm below Rt ear, 1cm below Rt. law, 6cm below chin,
5cm below Lt law, 5cm below left ear and 8 cm above lomum notch,
Total circumference of neck is 29cm.
2. C2 C3 vertebra found fracture and Hyoid bone found intact.
8. Thereafter, Investigating Officer examined first informant and other witnesses under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
Witnesses so examined have supported the FIR.

On the basis of above and other material collected by Investigating Officer during course of investigation, he came to the conclusion that Ikrar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135441137/
2 complicity of named accused is fully established in the crime in question.

sentences.text: He, accordingly, submitted the charge sheet dated 10.08.2021 whereby named accused has been charge sheeted under Sections 498A, 323, 304-B IPC and Sections 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station- Kithore, District- Meerut.
9. Learned counsel for applicant contends that though applicant is the husband of deceased, a named and charge sheeted accused yet he is liable to be enlarged on bail.

The marriage of the applicant with the deceased was solemnized on 20.02.2019, whereas, the occurrence giving rise to the present criminal proceedings has occurred on 01.05.2021 i.e. after expiry of a period of more than two years.
During this period, there is nothing on record to show that the deceased was tortured for non-fulfilment of additional demand of dowry or otherwise.

The bona-fide of the applicant is also explicit from the fact that the autopsy surgeon, who conducted the autopsy of the body of deceased did not find any other external ante-mortem injuries on the body of deceased except for the ligature mark.
Since, prima facie the death of the deceased is a suicidal death therefore, the applicant is not liable to be awarded the maximum sentence under Section 304B I.P.C. in case he is convicted.
10. Even otherwise, applicant is a man of clean antecedents having no criminal history to his credit except the present one.
Applicant is in jail since 01.06.2021.
As such, he has undergone more than 2 years and 8 months of incarceration.
The police report in terms of Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. has already been submitted, therefore, the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution against applicant stands crystallized.
However, up to this stage, no such circumstance has emerged on record necessitating the custodial arrest of the applicant during the pendency of trial.
To buttress his submission, he has relied upon the judgment of Supreme Court in Sumit Subhashchandra Gangwal Vs. State of Maharashtra, 2023 LiveLaw (SC) 373 (Paragraph 5),

entities.text: Sumit Subhashchandra Gangwal Vs. State of Maharashtra, 2023 LiveLaw (SC) 373 (Paragraph 5)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is further contended by the learned counsel for applicant that aforementioned charge sheet dated 10.08.2021 was submitted,
cognizance was taken upon same by the concerned Magistrate.
However, as offence complained of is exclusively triable by court of Sessions, concerned Magistrate, consequently committed the case to the court of Sessions.
The framing of charge order was passed against applicant on 20.04.2023.
The first informant Jameel appeared before court below as PW1 and his statement in chief was recorded on 25.10.2023.

However, since then he has been exceeding the process of the court consequently,
the examination-in-chief of even PW1 has not yet taken place.
On the above premise, it is thus urged that there is delay in the proceeding of trial.
Since the applicant is under custody, therefore, he cannot be said to be responsible for the delay in the proceeding of the trial.
On the cumulative strength of above, he therefore, contends that applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
In case, the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.
11. Per contra, the learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail.
He submits that since applicant is the husband of the deceased, a named and charge sheeted accused, therefore, he does not deserve any indulgence by this Court.
The death of the deceased has occurred within 7 years from the date of her marriage in the house of the applicant.

Since, the applicant is an inmate of the house and also the husband of the deceased, therefore, the burden is upon the applicant to not only explain the manner of occurrence but also is innocence in terms of Sections 106 and 113B of the Evidence Act.
Ikrar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135441137/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3 However, applicant has miserably failed to discharge the said burden up to this stage.
It is thus urged that no sympathy be shown by this Court in favour of applicant.

However, the learned A.G.A.
could not dislodge the factual and legal submissions urged by the learned counsel for applicant in support of this repeat application for bail with reference to the record at this stage.

12. Having heard, the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State, upon perusal of record, evidence, nature and gravity of offence, accusations made and complicity of accused coupled with the fact that marriage of the applicant with the deceased was solemnized on 20.02.2019,
whereas, the occurrence giving rise to the present criminal proceedings has occurred on 01.05.2021 i.e. after expiry of a period of more than two years, there is nothing on record to show that physical and mental cruelty upon the deceased in the interregnum for non fulfillment of the demand of additional dowry, the death of the deceased is a suicidal death inasmuch as per the autopsy surgeon,
who conducted the autopsy of the body of deceased, the cause of death is Asphyxia as a result of ante-mortem hanging, the bona-fide of the applicant is also explicit from the fact

that the except for the ligature mark, no other external ante-mortem injury was found on the body of the deceased,
prima facie the death of the deceased is a suicidal death, applicant is not liable to be awarded the maximum sentence under Section 304-B IPC in case of conviction, the clean antecedents of applicant, the period of incarceration undergone, the police report in terms of Section 173(2) Cr.P.C.
has already been submitted, therefore, the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution against applicant stands crystallized, yet the learned A.G.A. could not point out any such circumstance from the record necessitating the custodial arrest of applicant during the pendency of trial, the judgment of Supreme Court in Sumit Subhashchandra Gangwal (Supra), the framing of charge order was passed against applicant on 20.04.2023, upto this stage, one only prosecution witness has appeared on 25.10.2023, the statement in chief of PW1 was recorded, but he has been avoiding the process of the court, his examination-in-chief has not been recorded yet, the lackadaisical approach on the part of the prosecution in pursuing the trial, therefore, irrespective of the objections raised by the learned A.G.A. in opposition to the present application for bail, but without making any comments on the merits of the case, applicant has made out a case for bail.
13. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

14. Let the applicant-Ikrar, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) THE APPLICANT SHALL FILE AN UNDERTAKING TO THE EFFECT THAT HE/SHE SHALL NOT SEEK ANY ADJOURNMENT ON THE DATE FIXED FOR EVIDENCE WHEN THE WITNESSES ARE PRESENT IN COURT.
IN CASE OF DEFAULT OF THIS CONDITION, IT SHALL BE OPEN FOR THE TRIAL COURT TO TREAT IT AS ABUSE OF LIBERTY OF BAIL AND PASS ORDERS IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW.
(ii) THE APPLICANT SHALL REMAIN PRESENT BEFORE THE TRIAL COURT ON EACH DATE FIXED, EITHER PERSONALLY OR THROUGH HIS/HER COUNSEL.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4 IN CASE OF HIS/HER ABSENCE, WITHOUT SUFFICIENT CAUSE, THE TRIAL COURT MAY PROCEED AGAINST HIM/HER UNDER SECTION 229-A IPC.

(iii) IN CASE, THE APPLICANT MISUSES THE LIBERTY OF BAIL DURING TRIAL AND IN ORDER TO SECURE HIS/HER PRESENCE PROCLAMATION UNDER SECTION 82 CR.P.C., MAY BE ISSUED AND IF APPLICANT FAILS TO APPEAR BEFORE THE COURT ON THE DATE FIXED IN SUCH PROCLAMATION, THEN,
THE TRIAL COURT SHALL INITIATE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST HIM/HER, IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW, UNDER SECTION 174-A IPC.
(iv) THE APPLICANT SHALL REMAIN PRESENT, IN PERSON, BEFORE THE TRIAL COURT ON DATES FIXED FOR (1) OPENING OF THE CASE, (2) FRAMING OF CHARGE AND (3) RECORDING OF STATEMENT UNDER SECTION 313 CR.P.C.

IF IN THE OPINION OF THE TRIAL COURT ABSENCE OF THE APPLICANT IS DELIBERATE OR WITHOUT SUFFICIENT CAUSE, THEN IT SHALL BE OPEN FOR THE TRIAL COURT TO TREAT SUCH DEFAULT AS ABUSE OF LIBERTY OF BAIL AND PROCEED AGAINST THE HIM/HER IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW.
(v) THE TRIAL COURT MAY MAKE ALL POSSIBLE EFFORTS/ENDEAVOUR AND TRY TO CONCLUDE THE TRIAL WITHIN A PERIOD OF ONE YEAR AFTER THE RELEASE OF THE APPLICANT.

15. However, it is made clear that any wilful violation of above conditions by the applicant, shall have serious repercussion on his bail so granted by this Court and the trial court is at liberty to cancel the bail, after recording the reasons for doing so, in the given case of any of the condition mentioned above.

13. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.
14. Let the applicant-Ikrar, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) THE APPLICANT SHALL FILE AN UNDERTAKING TO THE EFFECT THAT HE/SHE SHALL NOT SEEK ANY ADJOURNMENT ON THE DATE FIXED FOR EVIDENCE WHEN THE WITNESSES ARE PRESENT IN COURT.
IN CASE OF DEFAULT OF THIS CONDITION, IT SHALL BE OPEN FOR THE TRIAL COURT TO TREAT IT AS ABUSE OF LIBERTY OF BAIL AND PASS ORDERS IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW.
(ii) THE APPLICANT SHALL REMAIN PRESENT BEFORE THE TRIAL COURT ON EACH DATE FIXED, EITHER PERSONALLY OR THROUGH HIS/HER COUNSEL.
4 IN CASE OF HIS/HER ABSENCE, WITHOUT SUFFICIENT CAUSE, THE TRIAL COURT MAY PROCEED AGAINST HIM/HER UNDER SECTION 229-A IPC.
(iii) IN CASE, THE APPLICANT MISUSES THE LIBERTY OF BAIL DURING TRIAL AND IN ORDER TO SECURE HIS/HER PRESENCE PROCLAMATION UNDER SECTION 82 CR.P.C., MAY BE ISSUED AND IF APPLICANT FAILS TO APPEAR BEFORE THE COURT ON THE DATE FIXED IN SUCH PROCLAMATION, THEN,
THE TRIAL COURT SHALL INITIATE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST HIM/HER, IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW, UNDER SECTION 174-A IPC.
(iv) THE APPLICANT SHALL REMAIN PRESENT, IN PERSON, BEFORE THE TRIAL COURT ON DATES FIXED FOR (1) OPENING OF THE CASE, (2) FRAMING OF CHARGE AND (3) RECORDING OF STATEMENT UNDER SECTION 313 CR.P.C.
IF IN THE OPINION OF THE TRIAL COURT ABSENCE OF THE APPLICANT IS DELIBERATE OR WITHOUT SUFFICIENT CAUSE, THEN IT SHALL BE OPEN FOR THE TRIAL COURT TO TREAT SUCH DEFAULT AS ABUSE OF LIBERTY OF BAIL AND PROCEED AGAINST THE HIM/HER IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW.
(v) THE TRIAL COURT MAY MAKE ALL POSSIBLE EFFORTS/ENDEAVOUR AND TRY TO CONCLUDE THE TRIAL WITHIN A PERIOD OF ONE YEAR AFTER THE RELEASE OF THE APPLICANT.
15. However, it is made clear that any wilful violation of above conditions by the applicant, shall have serious repercussion on his bail so granted by this Court and the trial court is at liberty to cancel the bail, after recording the reasons for doing so, in the given case of any of the condition mentioned above.
